clusters.name: Your stepfather Desmond joining the household, 1987
clusters.reason: Around the time you were beginning secondary school in 1987, three shifts pile up close together: your distance from Desmond, your warmth toward your dad, and your anxiety about making the city chess squad. Your stepmother's separation from your father over the question of a baby sits among these months as well. The period holds shifts in how you were relating to the men around you and how you were coping with new pressures at school.

clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Within five years from early 1989, when your grandfather returned to the family after years away, to early 1994, a long climb of trouble built without settlement between the steps. Around your grandfather's death in June 1991 and the months after, shifts pile up: you leaned hard on Rafe, your wrist injury stopped your playing and sent your anxiety and functioning down, you and Rafe fought and he left, you were getting high, and by early 1992 you were lost and low. Your grandmother's thyroid surgery followed nearby. Your mother's wedding to Desmond in October 1992 sits within the months when you were drifting through a bleak year at community college. Once you found your drive again with your exchange to Portugal in early 1994, the period settled. Your father's return and your move to the rebuilt house, your sister's birth, and your grandfather's death itself are the changes that opened this long disturbance.

clusters.name: Your separation from Joelle, 1998–1999
clusters.reason: In 1998 and 1999, around your relationship with Joelle and its end, two shifts that count sit close: your insomnia worsening before concerts though you were playing your best, and your shift toward therapy with Victor after the split. These two shifts stand beside each other with no one else's trouble showing in these months, so they are enough to hold the period.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's death and your separation from Marisol, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: From autumn 2001 to early 2004, your life fractured around two losses: your grandmother's bowel cancer diagnosis in 2001 or 2002 and your breakup with Marisol in October 2003. Around late 2001 you began running out of steam for performing and felt your anxiety and functioning fall; by early 2002 you had a disastrous audition and were done with performing. You were on poor terms with your family and left Thornbury for Gull Harbour. You met Marisol that winter and moved to Fenwick with her, but within months you split. You sank into deep depression through that winter, returned to Thornbury bunking with friends, could not face your family, and your anxiety rose. By late 2003 and early 2004, with support from your friends and your return to therapy with Victor, your functioning began to lift. Your grandmother spent her final months in your parents' home and died in February 2004. The period's opening sits in the months when your career was ending and your grandmother was being treated.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death and the cutoff from your mother, 2008–2010
clusters.reason: Within two years from early 2008, when you were at the lodge building with Silas before nursing school, to early 2010, a series of shifts in how you were relating to your mother piled up. Around July 2008 you were too drained to speak with her, she pressed you to visit against your wishes, and you kept the door shut on her visit. When you left for nursing school in August 2008, you stopped speaking to your mother entirely; the silence held for roughly a year. Your grandmother Lorna died in January 2008, and your grandfather Clifford died around the same time. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke in early 2009. During this same period, births in Wren's family began: her nieces Poppy and Max in 2010. The cut from your mother opened after months of distance at the lodge, not on a single date, but the timing—your grandmother's deaths, your move to nursing school—marks the boundary where contact became impossible.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren and your sister's first pregnancy, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: From your wedding to Wren in March 2017 through late October 2019, shifts pile up that touch every relationship in your life. Shortly after you married, you saw your mother a bit less as Wren's family came along. Your sister Tara, living far away for her airline work, was expecting her first baby by October 2019. In that same month, Wren became swamped with events—a street party, a fundraising dinner, her mother's retirement at the lake—and your anxiety and her functioning fell; you overfunctioned laying out a plan to settle her. She stays fused with her father and brother, talking to them constantly. Around the lake house weekend for her mother's retirement, you woke from the small hours with no more sleep and felt you didn't belong; Wren's anxiety rose as she sensed your distance on the drive home. Your own baseline anxiety has climbed steadily since at least 2019 with the sense that you ought to be driving your projects forward, though your job steadied and paid well. You have been aiming for shorter, more regular calls with your mother to keep contact from piling up into tension. This period holds the strains opened by the two families joining and the new pressures that came with them.
